recentItems.title: WEVV 44News at Noon (Full), 9/11/2026 (Final Newscast from Carpenter Street)
recentItems.description:
JOIN BROADCAST PLAZA TODAY, DISCORD'S MEDIA DISCUSSION COMMUNITY — http://bit.ly/S31MA

Complete 12pm newscast from the Gray-owned, former Allen CBS affiliate in Evansville, Indiana. Recorded on Friday, September 11, 2026.

A week after Gray ended separate newscast production for its Huntsville, Alabama station it bought from Allen, it is now doing the same thing in Evansville. WEVV will now simulcast the newscasts of Gray's existing NBC affiliate, WFIE, complete with the "14 News" branding. That being said, WEVV's news director is the one who is actually running the combined news operation since WFIE's left for family reasons. Some WEVV talent was retained for WFIE, and they can be seen on WFIE's site.

WEVV began as an independent, was the market's original FOX affiliate, added news in 1992, flipped to CBS in 1995, and stopped doing news in 2001. New ownership re-added news in 2015, this time from WTVW's former longtime studio on Carpenter Street. Basically Nexstar bought out ComCorp and was forced to spin off WEVV due to market concentration concerns since they already owned or controlled both WTVW and WEVV. Apparently, Nexstar threw in the abandoned WTVW studio as part of the deal. The former WEVV studio was then sold to local PBS affiliate WNIN.

Byron Allen bought DuJuan McCoy's stations in 2019, which gave him the capital to buy WISH from Nexstar when they had to divest it. This also market Allen's entry into broadcasting. Allen slowly stripped away WEVV's resources as the company had to make cuts due to a massive debt load. In 2025, this debt load became bad enough that it prompted Allen to finally sell. For now they retain some stations that Gray didn't want for various reasons, and sold them the rest, some in overlap markets like this, and others in markets new to Gray.

So basically, the market concentration concerns regulators had a decade earlier were not present this time, mainly because of an administration change as well as the declining linear television audience.

Gray took control of this and other Allen stations in May and immediately began resource sharing with WFIE though they allowed WEVV's separate newsroom to stay open through now. As mentioned above, WFIE retained a few WEVV anchors who joined the WFIE team. It went the other way too: the anchor seen here is a WFIE employee and was part of that station before the merger. I heard they had a WFIE reporter anchoring the last show so the WEVV people could finish training over at WFIE.

I guess this was inevitable and the market is now back to two TV newsrooms which was its status from 2011-2015 after Nexstar merged WTVW into WEHT. At the beginning of this century, it had four.

Graphics are from Hothaus Creative with some heavy in-house modifications, music was "Guardian" from Stephen Arnold Music, and Glenn Hansen was the voiceover artist (which in this case I'm OK with him disappearing here because he's added so many Nexstar stations).

Anchored by Emma Beck and weather from Weather Channel meteorologist Tom Sater (Gray had a transition agreement with previous owner Allen to continue to use them, but it ends this month; Allen had replaced mets at most of its station either partially or fully with this hub out of Atlanta, with some exceptions like WAAY, WTVA, and WKOW allowed to keep a full staff of local mets). Includes several news reports.

Commercials and promos have been retained.

recentItems.title: WAAY 48 News at 11:00 AM Open, 9/8/2026 (Now Produced by WAFF)
recentItems.description:
Open from the 11am newscast on Gray's ABC affiliate in Huntsville, Alabama, recorded on Tuesday, September 8, 2026.

As mentioned in a previous upload, WAAY shut down production on its Monte Sano studio on Friday, September 4, with the 11am newscast being the last to continue remaining separate from WAFF. WAAY had already switched to WAFF for the rest of its newscasts the month before. This was due to needing to wait for The Kelly Clarkson Show on WAFF to end first so their lifestyle show "Tennessee Valley Living" could be moved from 11am to 3pm for the new fall season. This then allowed WAFF to free up its studio to take on the new 11am newscast. It should be noted that WAFF itself does not air this newscast, and has opted for syndicated programming in this hour ("In Depth with Graham Bensinger" and "InvestigateTV") rather than simulcasting.

For whatever reason, Gray's local management in Huntsville decided to adopt WAFF's news branding for both station.

The 11am newscast continues to be anchored by Demetria Green who came over from WAAY. Green will also be joining WAFF's relocated lifestyle show as the new co-host at a later date (she was not on Tuesday's edition despite being present for the 11am news). She also does reporting for the later newscasts.

The look is the same as WAFF's shows: GrayONE with a modified version of WBRC's opening sequence, "Guardian" from Stephen Arnold Music as their theme, and Dave Hoffmann as voiceover.

Anchored by Demetria Green.

recentItems.description:
Open from the newly launched 7pm newscast on Gray's Fox affiliate in Lansing, Michigan, recorded on Tuesday, September 8, 2026. Produced by its sister NBC affiliate in town, WILX.

Gray received this station and one in Lafayette, Louisiana as part of a swap earlier this year with Scripps, in which they received three Intermountain West markets in exchange. A couple months after Gray's WILX took over the station, WSYM's newsroom merged into WILX's, and all of their newscast slots were replaced with simulcasts or new productions from WILX. This is one of the new shows WILX added for WSYM, since WILX already runs Wheel and Jeopardy in the 7pm hour. This was the debut show for it.

Open from the 5am hour of the morning newscast on Scripps' NBC and ABC affiliates in Grand Junction, Colorado, recorded on Thursday, September 10, 2026.

On Wednesday, the station got a new look as its new corporate owner makes its mark on the station.

On May 15, Scripps and Gray completed their exchange of assets which involved this station and its sister Fox affiliate KSVT, KKCO/KJCT in Grand Junction, and KKTV in Colorado Springs from Gray, and WSYM in Lansing and KATC in Lafayette from Scripps. Grand Junction is a new market for Scripps, in the others the receiving company already owned a station there or would be buying a station there in the case of Lafayette, Louisiana.

This week, all of the stations Scripps got in this swap picked up "The Keeper" graphics and their custom music from 11 One/Music. The stations kept Eric Gordon as their voiceover. They only got GrayONE last year so it didn't last very long in Grand Junction.

recentItems.title: WAAY 31 News Midday (Full), 9/4/2026 (Final Newscast from Monte Sano)
recentItems.description:
JOIN BROADCAST PLAZA TODAY, DISCORD'S MEDIA DISCUSSION COMMUNITY — http://bit.ly/S31MA

Complete 11am newscast from the Gray-owned, former Allen ABC affiliate in Huntsville, Alabama. Recorded on Friday, September 4, 2026.

As much as I hate typing this, WAAY had fallen so much that this was inevitable. WAAY was historically the market leader. Once the local Smith family chose to sell in 1999, a string of low budget owners purchased the station. Because of this, as well as investments by their competition, WAAY fell from first to last where it remains now. The Smith family were great owners, but the worst mistake they made was not choosing to sell, but selling to GOCOM rather than a company that would have respected their legacy and made further investments.

This isn't the first time WAAY would be sold to its competition. Ten years ago, WAAY almost consolidated with WAFF when its then owner, Calkins Media, decided to sell its broadcast group to Raycom Media. Raycom of course already owned the NBC affiliate, WAFF. But since a different administration was in charge of the FCC and DOJ back then, Raycom decided to spin off WAAY to avoid scrutiny, and Heartland entered the picture, preserving WAAY's independent newsroom. Three years later, Heartland sold their group to Byron Allen.

Six years later, and facing many financial issues along with a heavy debtload, Allen Media Group finally decided to put them on the market, and they found a buyer for most of them. Gray Media (who bought out Raycom in 2019 thus taking ownership of WAFF) bought them and WAAY was included the deal. Now with a different administration, one much friendlier to media consolidation, the deal was allowed to proceed, and in May, Gray took control of WAAY. Unsurprisingly, the WAFF management added oversight for WAAY (probably because WAFF is higher rated and they already worked for and were hired by Gray).

This began turning the wheels on merging the two operations into one. There were not massive layoffs immediately (unlike what happened in Indianapolis with WRTV), but rather cutbacks were phased over a period of months. Both WAFF and WAAY had reporters leave in the following months, both voluntarily and involuntarily, which helped get the numbers down that way. Some WAAY talent were retained for the new combined operation, some found positions at other Gray stations, and others (such as Jim Abath and Amber Kulick) were simply told their services were no longer needed.

On August 3, 2026, WAAY's news and weather apps were discontinued and merged into the apps of WAFF, along with redirecting WAAY's website into WAFF. The WAAY YouTube channel was also renamed "48 News" (which is confusing because it also coexists with WAFF's own YouTube channel named the same thing). WAAY then began simulcasting most of WAFF's newscasts on August 13. They opted for WAFF's existing branding, studios, and anchor lineup, with the exception of adding on WAAY's chief meteorologist Jeff Castle to the WAFF morning lineup (Jeff used to work at WAFF from 2002-2014).

However, there was one exception to this. Because of logistics, WAAY retained its separate midday newscast through Labor Day Weekend, with this broadcast, September 4, 2026, being their final newscast from atop Monte Sano.

Beginning Tuesday, September 8, WAFF will move its lifestyle show "Tennessee Valley Living", that was preventing them from doing an 11am newscast, to the 3pm timeslot to replace "The Kelly Clarkson Show", which will allow them to now do a live newscast from their studio for WAAY. This officially completes the consolidation of the two newsrooms. TVL will also add Demetria Green as a co-host for the show. Green will continue anchoring the midday news for WAAY as well from the WAFF studio. As mentioned above, Amber Kulick was not retained by the new owners and this was her final show.

recentItems.title: KMOV 32.1 First Alert 4 at 5:00 Open, ABC Launch Promo/Story, and Close, 9/1/2026 (First Day w/ ABC)
recentItems.description:
JOIN BROADCAST PLAZA TODAY, DISCORD'S MEDIA DISCUSSION COMMUNITY — http://bit.ly/S31MA

Open, a promo touting the station's new affiliation with ABC, a story inside the newscast doing the same thing, and the close from the 5pm newscast from the longtime CBS and now new ABC affiliate in St. Louis, Missouri owned by Gray. Recorded on Tuesday, September 1, 2026.

Announced in late July, KMOV began running ABC programming beginning September 1. Gray has made a significant investment in to KMOV since it took control, and this continues that. It was decided to give ABC its own channel position, 32.1 (previously used for the sports channel Midwest Matrix which was moved to a different channel), just two positions away from 30.1, KDNL, where ABC had resided in the market since 1995. Before that, ABC was on KTVI for decades. ABC has always been rated weakly in St. Louis, simply because KSDK was one of the nation's strongest NBC affiliates, and one of the most stable as well in terms of talent.

For now, the newscasts are just straight simulcasts of what appear on 4.1. There are apparently plans to add unique newscasts for ABC on 4.2 at some point, but due to the limited amount of time the station had to spin up ABC, this makes sense. And honestly, even though it's just a simulcast of news already appearing on a different channel, it's still a massive upgrade compared to before when no news was airing on ABC for the most part since 2001 aside from a couple attempts that barely qualified as local news.

The station's full time brand is "First Alert 4 on ABC" (despite social media accounts billing it as "ABC St. Louis", this has not been used on air). The station does not promote its limited syndicated programming, just the newscasts, avoiding the awkward wording of "Entertainment Tonight, weeknights at 6 on First Alert 4 on ABC". Syndicated programming also does not contain a bug.

Graphics are GrayONE, music is "CBS Local" from Stephen Arnold Music, and Drew Patterson (locally based in the market, the main reason they switched to him) is the voiceover artist.

Anchored by Cory Stark and weather from chief meteorologist Steve Templeton.
